messages:
Maya: FYI, Mediva POC hit repeated 429s during a bulk embeddings import around 23:45 PST. Customer saw spikes and an unexpected $38.72 usage line on their trial invoice. Can we swarm?
Drew: can you paste tenant id + route + model + sample request ids?
Maya: tenant=mediva-llm, route=/v1/embeddings, model=text-embed-3-small, example req=req_f9d3a. They ran ~30k docs with concurrency=8 via websocket uploader. Logs: 
```
2025-01-18T07:45:12Z [rate-limiter] tenant=mediva-llm route=/v1/embeddings status=429 burst_remaining=0 token_bucket=0.05
2025-01-18T07:45:12Z [ingest] req=req_f9d3a client=mediva-importer streams=8 tokens=1760
2025-01-18T07:45:12Z [billing] tenant=mediva-llm tokens_charged=1784
```
Maya: they said they batch 150 docs per stream.
Sam: pulling rate-limiter traces now. initial hypothesis: small burst window + simultaneous websocket streams causing token bucket exhaustion and some double-counting edge in older runtime. Which runtime are they on?
Maya: hosted, pinned to runtime variant v1.4.0.
Drew: confirmed known issue: streaming accounting bug fixed in v1.4.2. If pinned to v1.4.0, they'll see fractional bucket leftovers and occasional overcharge.
Nina: customer needs a demo tomorrow morning. Can we temporarily raise their per-route cap and give an invoice adjustment?
DeployBot: tenant-update: applied route-cap change tenant=mediva-llm route=/v1/embeddings old=80 new=400 expires=2025-01-19T08:00:00Z by=oncall.sam
Sam: cap increased to 400rps for 24h. Monitoring: 10m after change 429s dropped to near zero.
BillingBot: invoice lookup: mediva-llm charge $38.72 on 2025-01-18. Credit request CR-2025-887 opened, awaiting finance approval.
Drew: engineering follow-up: schedule rollout of accounting fix to pinned hosted variants and add a quick migration note for customers pinned to older variants. I'll file ENG-5123.
Maya: customer confirmed demo success and asked for confirmation that fix will hit their variant. Nina, can you loop AE and legal on the support credit and contract note?
Nina: on it. will ask AE to get acceptance criteria for permanent cap increase if they convert.
Maya: marking thread resolved from POC troubleshooting perspective. Notes: root cause = streaming token-accounting bug on runtime v1.4.0; temporary cap bump applied; credit request opened.
thread_summary: Mediva POC encountered 429s and unexpected invoice charge during websocket embeddings import; triaged to streaming accounting bug in older runtime. Temporary per-route cap raised and credit request opened; engineering to roll out fix to pinned variants.
